A fifth model, Fish Audio Drama 3, and a way to fix words in a generated clip without generating it again.

## ✨ New

- **Fish Audio Drama 3** (44.1 kHz): zero-shot cloning from a reference with its transcript, with lively, expressive delivery. It is a 35B mixture of experts; the studio runs it in 4 bits with most of its experts in the computer's memory, so it fits a 12 GB GPU (with 32 GB of RAM). Our own implementation, following SGLang-Omni's. Download it in the **Models** tab: a 4-bit build of the official weights (22 GB), its experts converted as HIGGS (rotated by a Hadamard matrix and rounded to 16 levels fitted to a Gaussian, no calibration data), which came closer to the official weights than plain 4-bit rounding or GPTQ. You can also choose to download the official weights and convert them on your computer (the same files; the official weights kept or removed), which is also what happens if the build can't be downloaded.
- **Directing Drama 3:** a **Style** for how to say the text (e.g. "with bright eager excitement"), tags at a spot ("[sighs]") or around words ("<whisper>…</whisper>": select the words, then pick the tag), and in Advanced a language hint and a length in seconds. Long texts are spoken in parts of whole sentences, each with the same reference, style and hints.
- **Edit words:** each clip in History has an **Edit words** button. Change, add or remove words and Drama 3 speaks only the changed words again, in the voice of the audio around them; the rest of the clip is kept as it was. It works on clips from any model. An edit takes about 2 s.
- **Saved Drama 3 voices:** with Drama 3's base model chosen, **Save as a voice…** keeps a name and a dataset's three best clips (or a clip of your own) as a voice in the list. It speaks with them whenever no other clip is given. Nothing is trained.
- **Models tab in groups:** text to speech, dataset tools and audio clean-up.
- **S2-Pro training on 12 GB GPUs:** the frozen slow transformer waits in the computer's memory and visits the GPU only when it is needed.

## ⚡ Faster

- Drama 3 synthesis: our own decoding step, each audio frame replayed as a CUDA graph, the 4-bit weights read straight by Triton kernels (the experts from the GPU or directly from the computer's memory), and the state after a voice's reference kept: about 0.6 s per second of audio on a 16 GB GPU, faster from the second line with the same voice.
- Long texts on S2-Pro: the audio codec now decodes long takes in pieces, with the same result, so its memory no longer grows with the length (in one pass a minute of audio needed about 4 GB more; on a full GPU, Windows then spills into much slower shared memory).

## 🔧 Fixed

- S2-Pro: English sentences of a long text are joined with a space.
- The CTC aligner runs its alignment step on the CPU, so it also works with CPU-only builds of torchaudio.

## ⚠️ Good to know

- **License:** Drama 3's weights are under the Fish Audio Community License: free below USD 500,000 yearly revenue, no hosted services, and consent is needed to clone a real person's voice. The Models tab and the third-party notices say so.
- Drama 3 needs 12 GB of GPU memory and 32 GB of RAM, and 22 GB of disk. It doesn't train: in our tests, with a reference its codebook decoder already renders a voice as well as the real recordings do.
- Drama 3's first line after loading compiles its decoding steps (a few seconds). On loading, transformers notes that two optional kernels aren't installed: they would speed up only a small part of reading the prompt.
- API: `POST /api/tts/edit` (a clip, its transcript and the new text) and `POST /api/loras/reference-voice` (a saved voice). `GET /api/engines` also lists what each engine's export holds (`package`), how many clips its voices' reference joins (`voice_reference_clips`) and its base model's repo (`base_repo`).
